record.original_question: Given two families of multivariate polynomials p1, ..., pk and q1, ..., qk, each represented by listing all monomials with nonzero coefficients and with no a priori bound on the number of variables or on the degrees, can one decide in deterministic fixed-parameter tractable time, parameterized by k, whether the identity ∏_{i=1}^k p_i = ∏_{i=1}^k q_i holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k be a positive integer parameter. The input consists of two families of multivariate polynomials with rational (or integer) coefficients,

  p_1, p_2, …, p_k   and   q_1, q_2, …, q_k,

where each polynomial is presented explicitly as a list of its monomials with nonzero coefficients (each monomial given by its coefficient and the exponent vector of the variables occurring in it). There is no a priori bound on the total number of variables that may appear among the p_i and q_i, nor on the individual degrees of these polynomials; the size of the input is the total bit-length of this monomial listing.

Decide whether the polynomial identity

  ∏_{i=1}^k p_i  =  ∏_{i=1}^k q_i

holds as an equality of formal polynomials.

Question: Does there exist a deterministic algorithm solving this decision problem in time f(k) · n^{O(1)}, where n is the input size and f is a computable function of k alone (i.e., is the problem in deterministic FPT when parameterized by k)?
artifact.status_search_result: The Polynomial Product Identity problem is listed as an open problem of Downey and Fellows. Surveys of the status of these open problems indicate it remains open whether the problem admits a deterministic FPT algorithm parameterized by k; a randomized FPT approach via polynomial identity testing is straightforward, but no deterministic FPT algorithm or hardness result resolving the question appears to be known.
